newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the southern U.S., rice prices were steady. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $20.50 to $21.00 per hundred lbs (CWT); medium grain traded mostly at $19.00; second heads were steady, and brewers remained in very tight supply with a few quotes at $13.75 to $14.50.
Rice by-products were uneven, bran was steady to $5.00 higher and millfeed was $3.00 higher to $2.00 lower.
In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly from $18.00 to $19.00 per cwt, second heads were steady, bran was 7.00-15.00 lower.
California rice ship loadings: For the week ending April 26, 1997 at the Port of Sacramento, there were no rice ship loadings.

Inspections of California rice for export: For the week ending April 26, 1997, there were no rice inspections. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 is 9,476,475 cwt compared to 6,178,783 cwt a year ago.
Feed by-products prices (dollars per short ton, FOB mills).
